s3.title: Shadow hypothesis · S3 long after negative funding
s3.label: Shadow hypothesis, not evidence; re-evaluate after ≥100 new trades
s3.ruleBad: Rule (frozen, ⚠ rule hash differs from registration)
s3.rule: When a funding settlement converts to an 8h rate ≤ −0.1%, go long at that hour's 1h perpetual close and exit at the close 72h later; one trade per coin at a time; net of taker fees 0.05%×2, slippage and funding paid while holding.
s3.registered: Registered {{time}} (only new signals after this count) · data: {{src}} · rule {{hash}}
s3.note1: Parameters per the director's decision: threshold 0.1%/8h, hold 72h. Report §3 item 3 says abs 0.05%, hold 24h/72h; since they differ, the director's 0.1%/72h is frozen here.
s3.note2: This rule is a post-hoc subset chosen after seeing hold-out data (report: 22 hold-out trades in 21 months, CI spans 0), so it can only be a hypothesis.
s3.note3: At the 0.1% threshold the report's hold-out had about 1 trade/month, so reaching 100 trades takes about 8 years; at 0.05% about 4 trades/month (about 2 years).
s3.note4: The report used Binance perpetual data; this uses the local market source's (current exchange) public funding rates and 1h perpetual closes.
s3.progressSub: Evaluated automatically per the report's method at 100 trades
s3.runningNote: Running figures before 100 trades are records, not evidence
s3.evalSub: Avg. net {{mean}} · CI [{{ci}}] · excl. best 3 trades {{ex}}
s3.empty: No signals yet (rates ≤ −0.1%/8h are rare; about 1 trade/month in the report's hold-out)

risk.backtestNote: Day-by-day/hour-by-hour review of the 19-coin hold-out (from 2025-01-09): single coin max 7%, gross exposure max 0.42, worst intraday −2.7%, max drawdown −8.1%, held longs never saw funding > 0.1%/8h, so no circuit breaker would trigger; the 31/31 acceptance uses the backtest engine and is not affected by these limits. In the training period (2021 bull market) the funding breaker would trigger, annualized 15.19% → 13.58%.
